previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now applies the anti-lag soft spark-skip ratio only while anti-lag is both enabled and actively engaged. Previously the configured skip ratio could suppress sparks whenever the limiter was evaluated, even with anti-lag disabled or not armed. The change is a firmware behavior fix with unit-test coverage; no tune migration is required, but anti-lag spark skipping should be re-verified on the bench.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU changed anti-lag soft spark skipping so the configured ALSSkipRatio is applied only when anti-lag is enabled and the anti-lag controller reports an active condition; otherwise the target skip ratio is zero. Drivers and tuners no longer lose sparks to a stale skip ratio when anti-lag is off or not armed, and skipping resumes when anti-lag re-arms. No tune migration is needed, but re-check anti-lag spark behavior on the bench because the change is validated only by unit tests, not on an engine.
evidence: firmware/controllers/engine_cycle/spark_logic.cpp: ALSSkipRatio now computed as antiLagEnabled && antilagController.isAntilagCondition ? ALSSkipRatio : 0.0f and applied via ALSsoftSparkLimiter.setTargetSkipRatio() at the top of onTriggerEventSparkLogic
firmware/controllers/engine_cycle/spark_logic.cpp: removed the unconditional setTargetSkipRatio(engineConfiguration->ALSSkipRatio) call from the per-event scheduling loop

last_sync.summary: Boost cut now keeps an active fuel cut when the MAP signal is missing, invalid, or non-finite, instead of releasing fuel. A missing or invalid MAP reading still cannot start a new cut. The existing 20 kPa release hysteresis is unchanged.

decisions.rationale: Boost cut now treats a missing, invalid, or non-finite MAP reading as neither a rising nor a falling event. If the cut is already active, fuel stays cut until a valid MAP reading falls 20 kPa below the configured Boost cut pressure. A missing or invalid MAP reading cannot start a new cut. No setting changes are needed; the existing Boost cut pressure value and its 20 kPa hysteresis still apply. Check MAP sensor wiring and diagnostics if fuel stays cut after boost falls.
evidence: firmware/controllers/limp_manager.cpp updateCutsBoostCut: adds Sensor::get(SensorType::Map), validMap = map && std::isfinite(map.Value), rising/falling booleans, and m_boostCutHysteresis.test(rising, falling)
unit_tests/tests/test_limp.cpp boostCut: missing and invalid MAP do not create a cut; missing and NaN MAP preserve an active cut; 79 kPa restores fuel
